title: Use colour and borders
summary: A background fills a box, while a border marks its edge.
introduction: A background fills a box, while a border marks its edge. Your task: Change the border from rounded-lg to rounded-none.

Explain the example for use colour and borders

blocks.text: A background fills a box, while a border marks its edge. Text needs enough contrast against its background.

These examples use Tailwind CSS 4 in a separate project. Install tailwindcss and @tailwindcss/cli. Put @import "tailwindcss"; in input.css and build with npx @tailwindcss/cli -i input.css -o output.css. Link output.css in HTML.

blocks.code:
<aside class="bg-yellow-100 text-yellow-950 border border-yellow-400 rounded-lg p-4">
  Bring water for the plants.
</aside>
blocks.title: Use colour and borders

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `p-4` adds inner space using Tailwind's spacing scale. It is a scale step rather than four pixels.
`rounded-lg` rounds the box corners. It changes the border shape, not the HTML meaning of the box.

blocks.text: The note has a pale yellow background, dark words, a yellow border and rounded corners.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Colour alone should not explain a message. Keep the actual reminder in words.
